pages.text: If you're reading this you got the letter, and it lied a little. The house is not $(italic)mostly standing$(). It has a chimney and opinions.$(br2)The only advice I'll give you all at once, so don't skip it: $(bold)do not look at the whole valley.$()
pages.title: Entry One

pages.text: It will flatten you. I did it once, in my sixtieth year, and sat on the step for a day and a half.$(br2)Look at the porch. Eleven feet of porch, weeds on it. Pull the weeds. Then look up and see if you want anything bigger.

That's the whole trick. I have used it on a broken wheel, a dead orchard and one genuinely terrible winter.$(br2)$(bold)The valley only ever needed one person to start.$()$(br2)The kettle's copper. It's older than me. Put it on.$(br)$(italic)-- J.K.$()
